papers.title: [Osseointegration click-on prosthesis following leg amputation].
papers.abstract: Since its introduction in 2009, more than 150 people in the Netherlands have received an osseointegration prosthesis following leg amputation. Serious complications such as septic or aseptic loosening and breakage of the implant are rare. In this article we highlight the results so far, the indications and contra-indications, our first experiences with patients who have undergone amputation due to vascular disease, and the future of osseointegration treatment in the Netherlands.

llm.relevance_to_user: 这篇论文关于截肢后骨整合假体的临床结果，未涉及增材制造、多孔结构或力学测试，与研究方向的关联性极低。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a clinical review of osseointegration prostheses with no LPBF fabrication, no porous structure design, no mechanical or fatigue testing, and no surface roughness analysis.

summary_en.motivation: To summarize clinical outcomes and future perspectives of osseointegration click-on prostheses in the Netherlands.
summary_en.method: A review of over 150 cases since 2009, including indications and complications.
summary_en.result: Serious complications (septic/aseptic loosening, implant breakage) are rare, with initial experiences in dysvascular amputees.
summary_en.validation: No experimental or mechanical validation; based solely on clinical case series.
